purpose: Scenario families for Synthea-grounded discharge reconciliation. These are not single scripted patients.
phase: clean cases only; no planted medication error

display_name_by_scenario_code.ENDOCARDITIS_OPAT: Outpatient parenteral antibiotic therapy after endocarditis

round1_design_requirements: Show baseline and the acute change.
Show a precipitant or a real evaluation that did not find one.
Establish important diagnoses after the work-up that supports them.
Show the treatment trajectory and the response, not only the word improved.
Support continue, stop, hold, restart, dose change, or new start from visible evidence.
Keep symptom, test, result, diagnosis, treatment, and response in a possible order.
A clean chart is not automatically a sufficient chart.

scenarios.clinical_reasoning_goal: Reconcile an initially uncertain outpatient list and decide which medicines continue, stop, or restart, distinguishing unknown medicines from intentional stops.
scenarios.synthea_eligibility: Alive adult with at least four single-ingredient outpatient products that match a curated regimen.
scenarios.required_longitudinal_context: Active outpatient medication products from the Synthea record.
scenarios.required_baseline: Baseline cognition when delirium is present, and the outpatient product list.
scenarios.required_presentation: The acute change that brought the patient in, without calling delirium the baseline.
scenarios.required_workup: The test that establishes the precipitant before that diagnosis is treated as known.
scenarios.required_response: Return of cognition or of the laboratory abnormality that justified the medication change.
scenarios.required_discharge_evidence: The history is resolved, and each changed medicine has a visible reason.
scenarios.reference_plan_rules: Derive continue, stop, or restart only from the visible list and the response.
scenarios.monitoring: Chemistry panel within 7 days when renal or electrolyte status changed.
citations: The Joint Commission National Patient Safety Goal on medication reconciliation; design guidance only, not a patient-specific fact.

scenarios.clinical_reasoning_goal: Explain an acute heart-failure hospitalization well enough to decide loop diuretic and renin-angiotensin therapy at discharge.
scenarios.synthea_eligibility: Alive adult with an active heart-failure condition, or, when that pool is small, an alive adult with cardiovascular disease plus a curated cardiovascular medicine. Prior heart failure is labeled synthea_longitudinal only when Synthea recorded it.
scenarios.required_longitudinal_context: Cardiovascular conditions and curated cardiovascular medicines.
allowed_precipitating_events: chest discomfort with negative ischemia testing
scenarios.required_baseline: Whether heart failure was already recorded, creatinine, and weight.
scenarios.required_presentation: Congestion on examination, oxygenation, and weight.
scenarios.required_workup: Radiograph, natriuretic peptide, and echocardiogram, with ischemia testing when the story needs it.
possible_treatment_trajectories: antibiotic limited to the infectious precipitant
scenarios.required_response: Weight, oxygenation, creatinine, and potassium after treatment.
scenarios.required_discharge_evidence: Euvolemia relative to admission and a visible reason for every changed cardiovascular medicine.
scenarios.reference_plan_rules: Do not sign the discharge list inside the resident chart. Restart of a held RAAS inhibitor requires recovered creatinine, acceptable potassium, and stable blood pressure.
scenarios.monitoring: Home weight and a chemistry panel within 7 days.
scenarios.follow_up: Heart-failure clinic and primary care within 7 days.
exclusion: no heart-failure condition and no compatible cardiovascular context
citations: Heidenreich PA et al. 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA heart failure guideline. Circulation. 2022;145:e895-e1032. Design guidance for work-up and medication review, not a source of this patient's laboratory values.

scenarios.clinical_reasoning_goal: Decide whether intravenous ceftriaxone continues after discharge once endocarditis has been established during the stay.
scenarios.synthea_eligibility: Alive adult with at least two active conditions. Synthea endocarditis is not required and was not present in this population. The infection is cliniproof_episode_generated.
scenarios.required_longitudinal_context: Enough chronic context to make an outpatient list meaningful. Home medicines are continued only when a curated regimen matches.
allowed_precipitating_events: bicuspid valve found on the echocardiogram
colonic-organism association with colonoscopy still pending
scenarios.required_baseline: Explicit statement that the longitudinal record did not already contain endocarditis.
scenarios.required_presentation: Fever and a murmur, before the diagnosis is named.
scenarios.required_workup: Blood cultures before antibiotics, organism, echocardiogram, and a source evaluation.
possible_treatment_trajectories: empiric ceftriaxone after cultures, then targeted continuation
scenarios.required_response: Defervescence and a negative clearance culture.
medication_transition_roles: do not invent an uncoded antibiotic
scenarios.required_discharge_evidence: Day of therapy, renal function supporting the 2 g dose, and a feasible outpatient infusion setting.
scenarios.reference_plan_rules: Continue the curated 2 g once-daily regimen. Do not claim Synthea supplied the infection.
scenarios.monitoring: Weekly chemistry panel and blood count.
citations: Baddour LM et al. Circulation. 2015;132:1435-1486. Ceftriaxone regimen also cited in medication_regimens.json.

scenarios.clinical_reasoning_goal: Start or intensify cytomegalovirus therapy only after testing, and continue the immunosuppression Synthea actually recorded.
scenarios.synthea_eligibility: Alive adult with renal-transplant history and extended-release tacrolimus matching TACROLIMUS_ER_1MG_DAILY. Patients without that curated match are excluded rather than assigned a different tacrolimus product.
scenarios.required_longitudinal_context: Transplant history and tacrolimus. Mycophenolate is not added merely because it is common.
scenarios.required_baseline: Transplant status and the statement that valganciclovir was absent unless the variant explicitly includes prior prophylaxis.
scenarios.required_presentation: Symptoms, not an established cytomegalovirus label.
scenarios.required_workup: CMV DNA, and biopsy when the syndrome is colitis. C. difficile testing when that exclusion is the variant.
possible_treatment_trajectories: increase from scenario prophylaxis to induction
scenarios.required_response: Symptom and volume or electrolyte response. Early viral clearance is not claimed.
scenarios.required_discharge_evidence: Creatinine in the range for full induction and a follow-up plan.
scenarios.reference_plan_rules: Do not label scenario prophylaxis as synthea_longitudinal.
scenarios.monitoring: Weekly blood count, creatinine, and CMV DNA.
scenarios.follow_up: Transplant clinic or infectious diseases within 7 days.
citations: Valganciclovir labeling for induction 900 mg twice daily and prophylaxis 900 mg once daily when renal function is preserved. Kotton CN et al. Transplantation. 2018;102:900-931. Design guidance only.

scenarios.clinical_reasoning_goal: Time fixation around the INR and decide warfarin restart versus a short further hold after surgery.
scenarios.synthea_eligibility: Alive adult age 65 or older with warfarin matching the curated 5 MG regimen and an atrial fibrillation, valve, or venous-thromboembolism condition.
scenarios.required_presentation: Hip pain and inability to bear weight, with the arrival INR.
scenarios.required_workup: Radiograph before the fracture label, and a repeat INR before the operating room.
possible_treatment_trajectories: hold warfarin for a wound hematoma
scenarios.required_response: INR decline, wound assessment, and mobility recommendation.
medication_transition_roles: warfarin hold then restart or continued hold
scenarios.required_discharge_evidence: Hemostasis or a described hematoma, INR, and disposition.
scenarios.reference_plan_rules: Enoxaparin does not continue as a chronic medicine. Restart and a short further hold are both represented when either is defensible.
scenarios.monitoring: INR within 3 days if warfarin resumes.
citations: Douketis JD et al. Chest. 2022;162:e207-e243. Perioperative anticoagulation design guidance, not a patient-specific INR.

scenarios.clinical_reasoning_goal: Hold warfarin for bleeding, identify a source, and decide whether restart is supported.
scenarios.synthea_eligibility: Alive adult with curated warfarin and an atrial fibrillation, valve, or venous-thromboembolism condition.
scenarios.required_baseline: Anticoagulation indication and the absence of chronic daily bleeding.
scenarios.required_presentation: Overt bleeding, heart rate, blood pressure, hemoglobin, and INR.
scenarios.required_workup: Endoscopy after resuscitation, before the source is named.
possible_treatment_trajectories: explicit unresolved hold after diverticular bleeding
scenarios.required_response: Hemoglobin nadir and recovery, vital-sign stabilization, and a fallen INR.
medication_transition_roles: warfarin hold then restart or continued hold
new pantoprazole for an upper source
stop ibuprofen when it was implicated
scenarios.required_discharge_evidence: Source, hemostasis, hemoglobin trajectory, and the persisting indication.
scenarios.reference_plan_rules: Do not treat a reasonable restart and a short further hold as a single mandatory answer.
scenarios.follow_up: Gastroenterology and anticoagulation follow-up within 7 days.
citations: Laine L et al. Am J Gastroenterol. 2021;116:899-917. Upper gastrointestinal bleeding guideline used as design guidance for endoscopy and acid suppression, not as a source of this patient's hemoglobin.
